chunk_findings.detail: `_clash_text` returns after the first live lease whose final pairs are non-empty, so the `keep` list is computed only from that first lease. With two live leases that clash on different requested globs (e.g. requested `["a.txt", "b.txt"]`; holder X clashes only on `a.txt` and changed paths overlap `a.txt`, holder Y clashes only on `b.txt`), the function returns `keep=["b.txt"]` and the user-facing message says `b.txt would be accepted`. That is wrong: `_clash_text` never checked Y, so `b.txt` would be refused separately.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_clash_text

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "for 0 min" in text` is time-dependent. `_setup` claims H1 and the test immediately checks that the refusal says the lease has been held for exactly `0 min`. In a slow or paused environment where more than 60 seconds elapse between the claim and the `run_cli(repo, "update", ...)` invocation, the holder age will be `for 1 min` (or more), causing this test to fail spuriously even when the fix is correct.

chunk_findings.detail: `changed` is the holder’s literal file paths from `completion.changed_paths`, but the change feeds each literal path into `conflicts`, which is a glob-pattern conflict check. A file named `docs/foo[1].txt` is a glob pattern that matches `docs/foo1.txt`, not the literal file. Given a holder changed `docs/foo[1].txt` and the requested glob is `docs/foo1.txt`, the actual paths do not overlap, so the update should be allowed. But `conflicts(["docs/foo1.txt"], ["docs/foo[1].txt"], shared)` treats the second string as a glob and reports a conflict, causing `_clash_text` to return a false refusal. The changed path must be matched literally (or escaped) rather than passed to `conflicts`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_clash_text

chunk_findings.detail: The new filters exclude any item whose `terminal` flag is true from `state.active_leases(...)` when detecting glob clashes. An item can be finished while its lease is still unreleased and still returned by `state.active_leases(...)`, so this change resolves that still-held contention automatically when the item finishes. The default in [D-lease-break-explicit] is that an active held lease is broken only through `ddflow claim --break`; this makes finished items effective implicit breaks.

chunk_findings.detail: When every requested glob is kept as a conflict, `keep == []`. The surrounding message does not guard that case, so for input `globs=["docs/**"]` it renders `"drop the overlapping ones ( would be accepted)"` — a false parenthetical because no requested glob would be accepted. The user-facing instruction is wrong in exactly the all-globs-conflict case.

chunk_findings.detail: The filter keeps a `pairs` entry whenever any actual changed path matches the requested glob, but it never checks whether that path is covered by a `shared_globs(cfg)` pattern. Example: config shared `docs/README.md`; other lease is `docs/**`; user requests `docs/**`; `conflicts(["docs/**"], ["docs/**"], shared)` still returns `("docs/**", "docs/**")` because the two globs overlap on non-shared paths, and the other holder's only changed path is `docs/README.md`. `any(GL.match(p, a) for p in changed)` is true for the shared README, so `_clash_text` returns a clash and refuses the update even though the only real change is an exempt shared file. Shared files should be inert for overlap, just as they already are when `conflicts` decides the glob pair in the first place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_clash_text changed-path filter

chunk_findings.detail: [D-lease-break-explicit] Filtering terminal items out of `live` means a live, unreleased lease on a finished item no longer counts as contention: `_clash_text`/`glob_clash` will return no clash for an overlapping update without `ddflow claim --break`. That makes lease breaking implicit in the contended/idle case that this decision says must remain explicit by default (`break_on_timeout` defaults to false); the automatic mode should only come from config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:live filtering in glob_clash/_clash_text

chunk_findings.detail: [D-lease-break-explicit] A live, unfinished holder with a clean worktree causes `holder_changed_paths(log, other)` to return `[]`, not `None`. In that case `changed is not None`, so every conflict pair is dropped and `_clash_text` returns `None` when no other holder remains. Example: item A holds `docs/**` but has changed no files yet; item B runs `ddflow update --globs docs/**`. The update is accepted without `ddflow claim --break`, auto-breaking an idle contended unfinished lease, which this decision says may be broken only via `--break`.

For input `globs=["docs/**"]` where `docs/**` is bad, it still renders a false parenthetical like “drop the overlapping ones ( would be accepted)”.

chunk_findings.detail: [D-lease-break-explicit] `_clash_text` drops all conflicts for a live, unfinished, contended lease when `holder_changed_paths` returns `[]` for a checked-out item with no file changes. Item A holds `docs/**` but has committed nothing; item B runs `update --globs docs/**`. `real` becomes `[]`, so `pairs` becomes `[]`, `_clash_text` returns `None`, and B proceeds without `ddflow claim --break`. That implicitly discards A's live idle lease even though `[lease].break_on_timeout` defaults to false and the decision says such a lease is broken only by `ddflow claim --break` unless the automatic project mode is enabled. The previous refutation only covered terminal/finished leases; this is an unfinished item with no changes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_clash_text

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier confirmed defect still holds. The visible hunk changes the caller and the refusal message, but it does not alter `_clash_text`’s changed-path filter to consult `shared_globs(cfg)`. Concrete failing input: config marks `docs/README.md` as shared; holder has lease `docs/**` and has changed only `docs/README.md`; user requests `docs/**`. `conflicts(["docs/**"], ["docs/**"], shared)` still returns an overlap on non-shared paths, so `_clash_text` still returns a clash and this branch still refuses the update even though the holder’s only actual changed path is covered by a shared glob. The hook and the update continue to disagree, which is the original B-shared-glob-update-waits case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_clash_text

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression suite never exercises the actual `leases.holder_changed_paths` logic end-to-end. This test monkeypatches `L.holder_changed_paths` to a fixed list, and the only other tests that allow a non-changed overlapping file also monkeypatch it. If `holder_changed_paths` is implemented incorrectly — for example, if it returns `item.lease.globs` or `["pkg/gates/**"]` instead of the holder’s real commit-touched path `pkg/gates/other.py` — the suite still passes because the non-mocked tests expect refusals for lease-covered paths, which an incorrect implementation would also produce. As a result, the original B-shared-glob-update-waits disagreement can remain: `ddflow update --globs mine.py,pkg/gates/x.py` would still refuse `x.py` even though the holder only changed `pkg/gates/other.py`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_glob_update_overlap.py:test_files_the_holder_does_not_change_are_allowed

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test file never exercises the hook path. The bug being fixed is defined by the hook and `ddflow update` disagreeing on lease coverage, but every test here goes through `run_cli update`, `AI.update`, `L._clash_text`, or `L.glob_clash` only. In the exact reported scenario, the hook can still accept the commit under the contended glob while all eight tests pass, so this change does not have a regression test for the half of B-shared-glob-update-waits that lets the commit through.
